title: PyraNet: A Multi-Layered Hierarchical Dataset for Verilog
problem: LLMs struggle to generate high-quality Verilog code due to lack of well-organized, high-quality training datasets and specialized fine-tuning methods tailored to hardware description languages.
motivation: Automatic HDL code generation with LLMs is promising but limited by poor dataset quality and lack of domain-specific training; improving Verilog generation quality is critical for accelerating hardware design.
method: PyraNet is an open-source collection of Verilog code (the language engineers use to describe hardware) organized in layers that progress from simple components to complete designs. When fine-tuning (customizing) large language models with this structured data, the layered organization helps the models learn the systematic patterns of correct hardware code. By training on organized examples rather than random data, the LLMs learn to generate Verilog that is both syntactically correct (follows language rules) and functionally correct (actually works as intended).
key_novelty: The core innovation is organizing Verilog code in layers—from simple circuits to complex designs—so that language models can learn to generate correct hardware code more effectively.
contributions: Open-source PyraNet hierarchical dataset for Verilog
Improved syntactic and functional correctness of generated code
limitations: Evaluation limited to VerilogEval platform; scalability to other HDLs (VHDL, Chisel) not addressed.
primary_theme: Hierarchical dataset and fine-tuning for improved Verilog code generation
